functions.name: Barcode.Detect
functions.signature: MBS( "Barcode.Detect"; Image { ; Type; ReturnType; TryRotation; Encoding } )
functions.description: Detects a barcode. We use zxing library internally and can only detect what this library handles. Internally all images are converted to grayscale. For you getting image, it's very important to get a sharp image. You may need to rotate or crop the image before sending into this method. Leave some white space around as some decoders don't want to start with black frame on the edge. The barcodes generated with Barcode.Generate often don't read as they have too little resolution (e.g. scale up by 3x) and no white border around (e.g. add 5 pixels). If special characters or umlauts are not recognized correct, you may have a wrong encoding. Most modern apps use UTF8 for encoding. For MacOS and iOS, you can also detect barcodes with CoreImage.Detect function, which is faster and can better find a barcode on a picture. Please note that Barcode.Detect uses zxing library, which can't read all barcodes well. For that reason we got Barcode.Scan using zbar library, which may be better. For FileMaker Go, please use PSoS and do the scan server side. Or build your own app based on the FileMaker iOS SDK with Xcode and embed the MBS Plugin for on device detection. See also Barcode.DetectAsJSON to get more detailed output of the result.

parameters.name: Image
parameters.description: The image to scan for a barcode. Can be container with image or an Image reference number from our GraphicsMagick image functions.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Which scanner to use. Supported types: Aztec, Codabar, Code39, Code93, Code128, DataMatrix, EAN8, EAN13, ITF, PDF417, QRCode, UPCA and UPCE. Pass All to scan for all types. Default is all.

parameters.name: ReturnType
parameters.description: A boolean to return the type as prefix. Pass 1 if you need prefix. Default is 0 for no prefix.

parameters.name: TryRotation
parameters.description: A boolean value. If 1, the plugin will rotate the image 90° to find vertical barcode. Default is true.

parameters.name: Encoding
parameters.description: The text encoding for text parameter. Default is UTF-8. Possible encoding names: ANSI, ISO-8859-1, Latin1, Mac, Native, UTF-8, DOS, Hex, Base64 or Windows. More listed in the FAQ .

functions.result: Returns barcode content text or error.

functions.name: Barcode.DrawBarcode
functions.signature: MBS( "Barcode.DrawBarcode"; PDF; symbology; Text; X; Y { ; Width; Height; Encoding } )
functions.description: Draws a barcode into a PDF page. The plugin uses zint library internally, so we include the zint manual in documentation. Possible symbologies: CODE11, C25MATRIX, C25INTER, C25IATA, C25LOGIC, C25IND, CODE39, EXCODE39, EANX, EAN128, CODABAR, CODE128, DPLEIT, DPIDENT, CODE16K, CODE49, CODE93, FLAT, RSS14, RSSLTD, RSSEXP, TELEPEN, UPCA, UPCE, POSTNET, MSIPLESSEY, FIM, LOGMARS, PHARMA, PZN, PHARMA_TWO, PDF417, PDF417TRUNC, MAXICODE, QRCODE, CODE128B, AUSPOST, AUSREPLY, AUSROUTE, AUSREDIRECT, ISBNX, RM4SCC, DATAMATRIX, EAN14, CODABLOCKF, NVE18, JAPANPOST, KOREAPOST, RSS14STACK, RSS14STACKOMNI, RSSEXPSTACK, PLANET, MICROPDF417, ONECODE, PLESSEY, TELEPEN_NUM, ITF14, KIX, AZTEC, DAFT, MICROQR, HIBC128, HIBC39, HIBCDM, HIBCQR, HIBCPDF, HIBCMICPDF, HIBCBLOCKF, HIBCAZTEC, AZRUNE, CODE32, EANXCC, EAN128CC, RSS14CC, RSSLTDCC, RSSEXPCC, UPCACC, UPCECC, RSS14STACKCC, RSS14OMNICC, RSSEXPSTACKCC, CHANNEL, CODEONE, GRIDMATRIX, EANXCHK, UPCACHK, UPCECHK, DOTCODE, HANXIN, VIN, MAILMARK, UPNQR and ULTRA.. For the size, be aware that some types like UPC codes have fixed size depending on content. Please use DynaPDF.SetPageCoords to set the coordinate system to TopDown before drawing barcodes. See also Barcode.SetOptions for further options. Deprecated. For newer development, please switch to DynaPDF.InsertBarcode function.

functions.name: Barcode.Generate
functions.signature: MBS( "Barcode.Generate"; symbology; Text { ; Width; Height; Rotation; Scale; Transparent; ShowText; Encoding } )
functions.description: Generates a barcode. The plugin uses zint library internally, so we include the zint manual in documentation. Possible symbologies: CODE11, C25MATRIX, C25INTER, C25IATA, C25LOGIC, C25IND, CODE39, EXCODE39, EAN8, EANX, EAN128, CODABAR, CODE128, DPLEIT, DPIDENT, CODE16K, CODE49, CODE93, FLAT, RSS14, RSSLTD, RSSEXP, TELEPEN, UPCA, UPCE, POSTNET, MSIPLESSEY, FIM, LOGMARS, PHARMA, PZN, PHARMA_TWO, PDF417, PDF417TRUNC, MAXICODE, QRCODE, CODE128B, AUSPOST, AUSREPLY, AUSROUTE, AUSREDIRECT, ISBNX, RM4SCC, DATAMATRIX, EAN14, CODABLOCKF, NVE18, JAPANPOST, KOREAPOST, RSS14STACK, RSS14STACKOMNI, RSSEXPSTACK, PLANET, MICROPDF417, ONECODE, PLESSEY, TELEPEN_NUM, ITF14, KIX, AZTEC, DAFT, MICROQR, HIBC128, HIBC39, HIBCDM, HIBCQR, HIBCPDF, HIBCMICPDF, HIBCBLOCKF, HIBCAZTEC, AZRUNE, CODE32, EANXCC, EAN128CC, RSS14CC, RSSLTDCC, RSSEXPCC, UPCACC, UPCECC, RSS14STACKCC, RSS14OMNICC, RSSEXPSTACKCC, CHANNEL, CODEONE, GRIDMATRIX, EANXCHK, UPCACHK, UPCECHK, DOTCODE, HANXIN, VIN, MAILMARK, UPNQR and ULTRA.. Please use EANX for EAN-2, EAN-5, EAN-8 and EAN-13. You may need to leave away the check digit for some barcodes. EAN-13 can be created with 12 or 13 digits, but for EAN-8, only pas 7 digits. This function returns an image reference for our GMImage functions. There you can either work on the image or simply store it in a container. On the end please free the image with GMImage.Release function. For the size, be aware that some types like UPC codes have fixed size depending on content. Or the size class for QRCode is calculated based on the text length. See also Barcode.SetOptions for further options. For MicroQR barcodes, you can use ECC Level 1 to 3, where 1 is default. Length is limited to only 35 characters minus space for ECC. You can use GMImage.SetDepth to customize the bit depth of the returned image before saving. Version 11.0 and further will default to 8 bit here, while 9.0 to 10.5 use 16 bit.

parameters.name: symbology
parameters.description: The symbology to use. e.g. EANX for EAN-13. Another possibility is to lookup the symbology code in the zint manual and pass the number here. EANX is 13 for example.

parameters.name: Text
parameters.description: The text to encode in the barcode.

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: The desired width of the barcode in pixels. Zero gives the auto size.

parameters.name: Height
parameters.description: The desired height of the barcode in pixels. Zero gives the auto size.

parameters.name: Rotation
parameters.description: The rotation. Can be 0, 90, 180 or 270.

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: The scale of the target image. Please use at least 4 for printing the barcode.

parameters.name: Transparent
parameters.description: 0: black on white 1: black on transparent background 2: white on black (new in 7.2) 3: white on transparent background (new in 7.2)

parameters.name: ShowText
parameters.description: Whether to show text. Use 0 to hide text or 1 to show text.

parameters.name: Encoding
parameters.description: The text encoding for text parameter. Default is UTF-8. Possible encoding names: ANSI, ISO-8859-1, Latin1, Mac, Native, UTF-8, DOS, Hex, Base64 or Windows. More listed in the FAQ .

functions.name: Barcode.LoadLibrary
functions.description: Loads the zbar library. Our Barcode.Scan function uses the open source zbar library. Since this library is licensed under LGPL, we can't embed it within the plugin, but you can ship it with your solution, either as a file you install with the plugin or as a file you store in a container and then export to a temp folder. If you have a libzbar64-0.dll in the FileMaker application folder, you can simply pass "libzbar64-0.dll" as path to load on Windows. We have libraries for you here: https://www.monkeybreadsoftware.com/filemaker/files/Libs/ With MBS Plugin v13.2, we implemented automatic loading of a zbar library if you don't call Bacode.LoadLibrary yourself. We look for libzbar64-0.dll on Windows, libzbar.so.0 on Linux and libzbar.dylib on macOS. If you have trouble with DLLs not loading on Windows, please check if you have new Visual Studio Runtime libraries installed. If you need more than one DLL, please use Process.SetDllDirectory to point to the folder to find the DLL files. On Linux if you get the error wrong ELF class: ELFCLASS32 if you try to load a 32-bit library into a 64-bit application. You may also get errors about version GLIBC_2.25 or similar if your libc library on the Linux installation isn't new enough for the loaded library.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: Native file path to the library. A dylib on macOS, a DLL file on Windows and a shard object on Linux wiht so extension.

functions.name: Barcode.Scan
functions.description: Scans for barcodes in a picture. Please use Barcode.LoadLibrary once in start script to load zbar library before using this function. Works best with black & white picture, so you may enhance contrast. ZBar is an open source software suite for reading bar codes from various sources, such as video streams, image files and raw intensity sensors. It supports many popular symbologies (types of bar codes) including EAN-13/UPC-A, UPC-E, EAN-8, Code 128, Code 39, Interleaved 2 of 5 and QR Code. ZBar is licensed under the GNU LGPL 2.1 to enable development of both open source and commercial projects. For FileMaker Go, please use PSoS and do the scan server side. Or build your own app based on the FileMaker iOS SDK with Xcode and embed the MBS Plugin and the zbar library for on device detection. The JSON array includes objects with following keys:

parameters.name: AllowedTypes

functions.name: Barcode.SetOptions
functions.description: Sets options for barcode creation. Creating a barcode will reset those options to zero for next barcode. For QRCode: Option1 is the ECC Level with values from 1 = low, 2 = middle, 3 = better, 4 high. Default is low. Option2 is version code from 1 to 40. Default is 0 to auto select. For MicroQR you can use ECC Level 1 to 3 as 4 is not supported. For Data Matrix: Option2 size from 1 to 30. 0 is auto. See table in zint manual pdf. Option3 can be 100 to force square size. e.g. below we set option3 to 100 to square, output options to 16 for reader init added and we pass some hex encoded characters in the JSON for Barcode.GenerateJSON function: {

functions.name: Barcode.WriteFile
functions.signature: MBS( "Barcode.WriteFile"; Type; Path; symbology; Text { ; Width; Height; Rotation; Scale; transparent; ShowText; Encoding } )
functions.description: Generates a barcode and writes to file. The plugin uses zint library internally, so we include the zint manual in documentation. Possible symbologies: CODE11, C25MATRIX, C25INTER, C25IATA, C25LOGIC, C25IND, CODE39, EXCODE39, EANX, EAN128, CODABAR, CODE128, DPLEIT, DPIDENT, CODE16K, CODE49, CODE93, FLAT, RSS14, RSSLTD, RSSEXP, TELEPEN, UPCA, UPCE, POSTNET, MSIPLESSEY, FIM, LOGMARS, PHARMA, PZN, PHARMA_TWO, PDF417, PDF417TRUNC, MAXICODE, QRCODE, CODE128B, AUSPOST, AUSREPLY, AUSROUTE, AUSREDIRECT, ISBNX, RM4SCC, DATAMATRIX, EAN14, CODABLOCKF, NVE18, JAPANPOST, KOREAPOST, RSS14STACK, RSS14STACKOMNI, RSSEXPSTACK, PLANET, MICROPDF417, ONECODE, PLESSEY, TELEPEN_NUM, ITF14, KIX, AZTEC, DAFT, MICROQR, HIBC128, HIBC39, HIBCDM, HIBCQR, HIBCPDF, HIBCMICPDF, HIBCBLOCKF, HIBCAZTEC, AZRUNE, CODE32, EANXCC, EAN128CC, RSS14CC, RSSLTDCC, RSSEXPCC, UPCACC, UPCECC, RSS14STACKCC, RSS14OMNICC, RSSEXPSTACKCC, CHANNEL, CODEONE, GRIDMATRIX, EANXCHK, UPCACHK, UPCECHK, DOTCODE, HANXIN, VIN, MAILMARK, UPNQR and ULTRA.. Please use EANX for EAN-8 and EAN-13. You may need to leave away the check digit for some barcodes. For the size, be aware that some types like UPC codes have fixed size depending on content. See also Barcode.SetOptions for further options. See FileDialog functions if you like to show a save dialog to pick a destination for the file path.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: Which file type to generate. Can be PNG, TIFF, JPEG, SVG or PS.

parameters.name: Path
parameters.description: The file path to use. Currently limited to 255 characters for SVG and PS.

parameters.name: symbology
parameters.description: The symbology to use. e.g. EANX for EAN-13.

parameters.name: Text
parameters.description: The text to encode in the barcode.

parameters.name: Width
parameters.description: The desired width of the barcode in pixels. Zero gives the auto size.

parameters.name: Height
parameters.description: The desired height of the barcode in pixels. Zero gives the auto size.

parameters.name: Rotation
parameters.description: The rotation. Can be 0, 90, 180 or 270.

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: The scale of the target image. Please use at least 4 for printing the barcode.

parameters.name: transparent
parameters.description: Pass 1 to have the white background being transparent.

parameters.name: ShowText
parameters.description: Whether to show text. Use 0 to hide text or 1 to show text.

parameters.name: Encoding
parameters.description: The text encoding for text parameter. Default is UTF-8. Possible encoding names: ANSI, ISO-8859-1, Latin1, Mac, Native, UTF-8, DOS, Hex, Base64 or Windows. More listed in the FAQ .

parameters.name: Type

$r

; Value:

( "
Clipboard.GetText
"; "JSON") ]

"; "") ]

functions.name: Clipboard.DetectFileMakerDataType
functions.description: Checks which type of data is in the XML. Returns the type as text: ValueList, Script, ScriptStep, Layout, CustomFunction, Table, Field or Layout12. Added new types Menu and MenuSet for MBS Plugin in version 12.2.

parameters.name: XML Text
parameters.description: The xml text to put on the clipboard.

functions.name: Clipboard.GetData
functions.description: Queries data from clipboard item. We look at the clipboard for a matching item with given type and return it in the format type you request. For server this will query the clipboard of the user account running the server app on the server computer and not the clipboard of any client.

parameters.name: ClipboardType
parameters.description: The clipboard type to query. On Windows can also be a number.

parameters.name: ResultType
parameters.description: How to return the data. Can be "hex" for hex encoded, "base64" for base 64 encoded, "text" for trying to read data as text, "file" for a container value containing a file or "image" for reading data as image.

parameters.name: Param1
parameters.description: For ResultType "file" the filename of the container value. For ResultType "image" the image type. Can be PNG, JPEG, GIF or BMP.

parameters.name: Param2
parameters.description: For ResultType "image", the file name of the image in the container value.

functions.name: Clipboard.GetFileMakerData
functions.description: Queries the xml text of a FileMaker layout/script object. The result is a XML text which you can store for later. The type can be ValueList, Script, ScriptStep, Layout, CustomFunction, Table, Field or Layout12. Pass auto as type in version 10.1 or newer to let the plugin look for all types and return the data found. For server this will query the clipboard of the user account running the server app on the server computer and not the clipboard of any client. Added type ValueList for FileMaker 16. For custom menus in FileMaker 17, please use Clipboard.GetText function. Warning: Some settings in script step for import, export or printer setup may not be preserved in copied content!

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: What element type to query. Can be "auto" for version 10.1 for automatic type selection.

functions.name: Clipboard.GetFiles
functions.description: Queries file paths on the clipboard. If you copy files in Finder or Explorer, you can use this plugin function to get a list of files. Returns native file paths, so you may need Path.NativePathToFileMakerPath function. For server this will query the clipboard of the user account running the server app on the server computer and not the clipboard of any client.

functions.name: Clipboard.GetHTMLText
functions.description: Queries styled text from clipboard as HTML. For server this will query the clipboard of the user account running the server app on the server computer and not the clipboard of any client. For macOS, if a webarchive is on the clipboard, the plugin will pick data from that webarchive. Safari puts a Webarchive on the clipboard if you do a copy to the clipboard. If text encoding is UTF-8, the plugin will automatically use this encoding as default unless you overwrite it.

parameters.name: Encoding
parameters.description: The text encoding for result. Default is Windows ANSI. Possible encoding names: ANSI, ISO-8859-1, Latin1, Mac, Native, UTF-8, DOS, Hex, Base64 or Windows. More listed in the FAQ .

functions.name: Clipboard.GetPDF
functions.description: Queries PDF in the clipboard. You can put result in variable or assign to a field. Returns empty value if clipboard does no contain PDF data.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: The filename to use for the container value. Default is clipboard.pdf

functions.name: Clipboard.GetPicture
functions.description: Queries a picture from clipboard. You can store image in a container field for example.

parameters.name: ImageType
parameters.description: The type of image to return. Either JPEG, PNG, GIF or BMP. Default is JPEG.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: The filename to use for the picture. Default is "image" with the extension matching the image type.

functions.name: Clipboard.GetRTFText
functions.description: Queries styled text from clipboard as RTF. For server this will query the clipboard of the user account running the server app on the server computer and not the clipboard of any client.

parameters.name: Encoding
parameters.description: The text encoding for result. Default is Windows ANSI. Possible encoding names: ANSI, ISO-8859-1, Latin1, Mac, Native, UTF-8, DOS, Hex, Base64 or Windows. More listed in the FAQ .

functions.name: Clipboard.GetStyledText
functions.description: Queries styled text from clipboard. For server this will query the clipboard of the user account running the server app on the server computer and not the clipboard of any client. Implemented for Windows with version 11.3 of MBS Plugin. If there is no styled text, we return empty text and you may use Clipboard.GetText then.

functions.name: Clipboard.GetText
functions.description: Queries clipboard content as text. Examples for type parameter: public.utf8-plain-text, CorePasteboardFlavorType 0x54455854, public.rtf,CorePasteboardFlavorType 0x75747874. For server this will query the clipboard of the user account running the server app on the server computer and not the clipboard of any client. You may want to use Text.ReplaceNewLine function with mode = 1 on the text to normalize line endings to what FileMaker expects. To query FileMaker’s XML for ValueList, Script, ScriptStep, Layout, CustomFunction, Table or Field, please check Clipboard.GetFileMakerData function.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: The data type. By default NSStringPboardType, but can be other Mac types. Mac only.

functions.result: The text from the clipboard. Empty if no text is there.

examples.label: Get text from clipboard:
examples.text_code:
MBS
("Clipboard.GetText")
Get text from clipboard:
examples.xml_code:

functions.name: DialogModifications.Uninstall
functions.description: Uninstalls the feature. You should call this when you no longer need the replacements. See also DialogModifications.Install .

functions.name: FileDialog.GetAllowMulti
functions.description: Queries whether multiple selection is allowed.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetAllowsOtherFileTypes
functions.description: Queries if other file types.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetCanCreateDirectories
functions.description: Queries whether the user can create directories.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetCanSelectHiddenExtension
functions.description: Returns a Boolean value that indicates whether the panel allows the user to hide or show extensions.
functions.result: Returns 1 when the panel allows the user to hide or show extensions; otherwise, 0.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetFilter
functions.description: Queries which filter is defined. Returns the values passed to FileDialog.SetFilter .

parameters.name: Selector
parameters.description: Which value to query. Can be MacFilter, WinFilter or WinLabels.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetInitialDirectory
functions.description: Queries the initial directory. Use Path.NativePathToFileMakerPath to convert to a FileMaker path if required.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetMessage
functions.description: Returns the message displayed in the save panel.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetNameFieldLabel
functions.description: Returns the string displayed in front of the filename text field.
functions.result: Returns initial text for the name field.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetNameFieldStringValue
functions.description: Returns the user-editable filename currently shown in the name field.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetPath
functions.description: Queries the native path with the given index. Use Path.NativePathToFileMakerPath to convert to a FileMaker path if required. Please note that in sheet mode ( FileDialog.SetUseSheet with 1), you need to wait for the trigger to be called before you can query paths.

parameters.name: Index
parameters.description: The index of the path.

  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text>get path from dialog:</Text>
  </Step>

    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS( "FileDialog.GetPath"; 0 )</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$npath</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">

  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">

    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$fpath</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text>Loop over all records:</Text>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="16" name="Go to Record/Request/Page">
    <NoInteract state="True"/>
    <RowPageLocation value="First"/>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="71" name="Loop">
    <Restore state="False"/>
    <FlushType value="Always"/>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text>Export files from this record</Text>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text>figure out file name</Text>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>GetAsText ( Container Batch Export::Test1 )</Calculation>

    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$name</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>

    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$name</Name>
  </Step>

      <Calculation>MBS( "Path.LastPathComponent"; $name )</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$name</Name>

functions.name: FileDialog.GetPathCount
functions.description: Queries number of file paths available. If multiple selection is enabled, this value can be bigger than one. If dialog was cancelled, this value is zero.
functions.result: Returns number of available file paths.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetPrompt
functions.description: Queries current prompt text.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetResolvesAliases
functions.description: Returns whether the panel resolves aliases.
functions.result: Returns 1 if alias files are resolved or 0 if not.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetShowHidden
functions.description: Returns whether the panel displays files that are normally hidden from the user.
functions.result: Returns 1 if hidden files are visible and 0 if not.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetTreatsFilePackagesAsDirectories
functions.description: Whether the panel displays file packages as directories.
functions.result: Returns 1 if enabled or 0 if disabled.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetUseSheet
functions.description: Queries sheet status.

functions.name: FileDialog.GetWindowTitle
functions.description: Returns the title of the panel.

// new matrix
matrix =

Matrix.New
"; 3; 4);
// add some content

MBS

Matrix.SetRow

r =
MBS

Matrix.SetRow

r =
MBS

Matrix.SetRow

MBS

Matrix.New

r =
MBS

functions.name: Matrix.ConvertDataType
functions.signature: MBS( "Matrix.ConvertDataType"; MatrixRef; DataType { ; FirstRow; LastRow; firstCol; lastCol } )
functions.description: Converts the data types. We loop over all rows in all columns for the range and convert the value to the given type. If you get data from FM.SQL.Execute , we have no FM.SQL.ConvertDataType as the rows are readonly. So please convert to matrix first and use FM.SQL.ToMatrix first and then use Matrix.ConvertDataType.

parameters.name: MatrixRef
parameters.description: The matrix reference number.

parameters.name: DataType
parameters.description: The new data type. Can be Number, Container, Date, Time, TimeStamp or Text.

parameters.name: FirstRow
parameters.description: The index of first row. Default is 0.

parameters.name: LastRow
parameters.description: The index of last row. Default is Matrix.Height -1.

parameters.name: firstCol
parameters.description: The index of first column. Default is 0.

parameters.name: lastCol
parameters.description: The index of last column. Default is Matrix.Width -1.

functions.name: Matrix.Evaluate
functions.signature: MBS( "Matrix.Evaluate"; MatrixRef; Expression { ; FirstRow; LastRow; firstCol; lastCol; Flags } )
functions.description: Evaluates an expression for each cell. You can change the value by doing a calculation in FileMaker syntax to change the value. Reference current value via "current", the current row via "row" and the current column via "column" as variable names. The result of the evaluate is written to the cell. May return error if expression is invalid.

parameters.name: MatrixRef
parameters.description: The matrix reference number.

parameters.name: Expression
parameters.description: The expression to evaluate. Can include "row", "column" and "current" as variables.

parameters.name: FirstRow
parameters.description: The index of first row. Default is 0.

parameters.name: LastRow
parameters.description: The index of last row. Default is Matrix.Height -1.

parameters.name: firstCol
parameters.description: The index of first column. Default is 0.

parameters.name: lastCol
parameters.description: The index of last column. Default is Matrix.Width -1.

parameters.name: Flags
parameters.description: Pass 1 to ignore results of expressions and not put them back in matrix. Pass 2 to continue after error (new in 13.5).

functions.name: Matrix.InsertOrUpdateRecords
functions.signature: MBS( "Matrix.InsertOrUpdateRecords"; MatrixRef; InsertFileName; InsertTableName; FieldNames; KeyFieldMapping )
functions.description: Insert or updates a lot of records queried from a database. Similar to FM.InsertOrUpdateRecordQuery , but taking records from a matrix. Copy can be from one database to other or within same database. Also from one table to other or within a table. Due to passing in new field names, you can even rearrange values from one column to other while copying. In the SQL you can use functions for sums or join data from several tables together to fill a new table. Filename parameters can be empty. Use FM.ExecuteSQL.LastErrorMessage and FM.ExecuteSQL.LastError to see error message. Reports an error if field name list doesn't match column count of the stored SQL result. Please remove from SQL statement and field names all fields which are globals or unstored calculations. For inserting records from other database (e.g. MySQL), please use SQL.InsertRecords function. You can specify fields and table via IDs and the plugin will lookup them for you at runtime. Table IDs and table names must be unique across all open files for this to work correctly. You can use GetFieldName() function to query field names and the plugin removes the table prefix with :: in the field name before passing it to SQL engine.

parameters.name: MatrixRef
parameters.description: The matrix reference number.

parameters.name: InsertFileName
parameters.description: The file name of where the insert table is inside. Can be empty to look for the table in all files.

parameters.name: InsertTableName
parameters.description: The name of the table to insert record into. Can be ID of table, so we lookup name by ID. Can be result of GetFieldName() function as we remove field name automatically.

parameters.name: FieldNames
parameters.description: A list of field names for the insert. Empty entries in the list are ignored. Can be ID of field, so we lookup name by ID. Can be result of GetFieldName() function as we remove table name automatically.

parameters.name: KeyFieldMapping
parameters.description: The list of field names with index to map keys. Please specify a list of key name=key index. The key name is the name of the field in the insert table and the index gives zero-based position in result set from SELECT query in 6th parameter. Field order in source and destination does not need to be the same.

functions.name: Matrix.InsertRecords
functions.signature: MBS( "Matrix.InsertRecords"; MatrixRef; InsertFileName; InsertTableName; FieldNames { ; StartRow; EndRow } )
functions.description: Inserts records in FileMaker database from records in memory. This function allows to easily copy a lot of records from a query in FileMaker database into a FileMaker table. Please provide field names in FileMaker. The order has to match those in the record set. Due to passing in new field names, you can even rearrange values from one column to other while copying. In the SQL you can use functions for sums or join data from several tables together to fill a new table. Use FM.ExecuteSQL.LastErrorMessage and FM.ExecuteSQL.LastError to see error message. Reports an error if field name list doesn't match column count of the query result. Function will fail if data types in source and dest fields do not match for assignment. e.g. date and time fields will not work, only timestamp fields. For insert from SQL Connection into FileMaker database, please use SQL.InsertRecords .

parameters.name: MatrixRef
parameters.description: The matrix reference number.

parameters.name: InsertFileName
parameters.description: The file name of where the insert table is inside. Can be empty to look for the table in all files.

parameters.name: InsertTableName
parameters.description: The name of the table to insert record into.

parameters.name: FieldNames
parameters.description: A list of field names for the insert. Empty entries in the list are ignored.

parameters.name: StartRow
parameters.description: The index of the start row in the current recordset. First row is 0.

parameters.name: EndRow
parameters.description: The index of the end row in the current recordset. First row is 0. Last Row would be Matrix.Height -1.

In the SQL you can use functions for sums or join data from several tables together to fill a new table. Reports an error if field name list doesn't match column count of the query result. Function will fail if data types in source and dest fields do not match for assignment. e.g. date and time fields will not work, only timestamp fields. For insert within FileMaker, please use Matrix.InsertRecords .

parameters.name: MatrixRef

functions.name: SharingPanel.SetScript
functions.description: Sets the script to call when sharing panel is done. In the script you can check with SharingPanel.Result , SharingPanel.ErrorText and SharingPanel.ErrorCode what happened. If the activity provides an answer, check SharingPanel.Item and SharingPanel.ItemCount functions to get them. With plugin version 6.0 or newer the script name can be a script ID number. In that case the plugin queries the script name for the given script ID. This allows to call scripts by ID and avoid problems if scripts are later renamed. Notice: FileMaker 19.2 adds a fmplugin extended privileges. If you have such an extended privileges to allow the plugin to trigger scripts, you need to grant permissions for it. If such a privilege is not defined, the plugin is allowed to trigger scripts. See FileMaker product documentation for details.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: The file name for the script to trigger.

parameters.name: ScriptName

functions.name: StoreRegistration
functions.signature: MBS( "StoreRegistration"; Licensee Name; Component; License Type; Expire Month; Serial number )
functions.description: Stores registration on Mac in preferences file of FileMaker so the plugin can auto register itself on startup of FileMaker. This is very useful for trainings where you want to preinstall license on FileMaker installations. Added Windows support in plugin version 4.4. You can clear the license with ClearRegistration function. Added Linux support for 7.5. Saves in preferences file on Mac and Linux, saves to registry on Windows. To store the registration on a FileMaker Server permanently, it is sufficient to call the StoreRegistration function only once by opening a file (e.g. the Registration.fmp12 file) with a OnFirstWindowOpen-Script and a single line of code like this: Set Variable [ $r; Value: MBS( "StoreRegistration"; $name; "Complete"; "5 seat"; $date; $code) ]. After opening it once and thus writing the registration file to the preference file, it can be closed and removed from the server. Currently on Windows the key is written encrypted to the registry into the HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\FileMaker\RegistrationMBS entry. On macOS and iOS, we write a RegistrationMBS entry into the com.filemaker.client.pro12.plist file or for Claris Pro into the com.claris.pro.plist file. For Linux the license is saved to /opt/FileMaker/FileMaker Server/MBS.license file. If you use this in a vertical solution, please make sure you update the license key before updating the plugin to avoid the user seeing an error dialog about an old license. Also make sure that every major update you make calls StoreRegistration with a new key to replace the old key stored in preferences. And consider getting a multi year update from us, so you only change license key every few years.

parameters.name: Licensee Name
parameters.description: This is the name of the person or organization that holds the license for the plug-in

parameters.name: Component
parameters.description: The component that was licensed. For example "Complete"

parameters.name: License Type
parameters.description: Seats purchased. For example, "1 seat", "10 seats", "Developer"

parameters.name: Expire Month
parameters.description: This is the month in which the serial will expire for new versions of the plug-in in YYYYMM format. Plug-in released before the end of that month will continue to work forever. New Releases after that date will require a renewal

parameters.name: Serial number
parameters.description: The license number

functions.name: SystemInfo.AppResourceUsageStatistics
functions.description: Queries application resource usage statistics for current application. The SystemInfo.AppResourceUsageStatistics function is a macOS-specific function that retrieves detailed resource usage statistics for the current process. It fills a versioned rusage info structure with metrics such as CPU time, memory footprint, disk I/O, and energy usage. This API is part of the libproc library and allows fine-grained performance monitoring, including per-QoS and power-weighted data, not available through standard POSIX interfaces. Our plugin returns this as JSON.

functions.name: SystemInfo.CPULoad
functions.description: Queries system load statistics. Returns a JSON with entries for system, user and idle. Those counters count up, so you may need to query several times and check deltas. The nice value is always zero for Windows.

examples.label: Query system load on macOS:
examples.text_code:
MBS
( "SystemInfo.CPULoad" )
Query system load on macOS:
Example result:
{
"system"
:
54822806
,
"nice"
:
0
,
"idle"
:
1143567712
,
"user"
:
78572673
}
examples.xml_code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS( "SystemInfo.CPULoad" )</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
</fmxmlsnippet>

examples.label: Query CPU Load:
examples.xml_code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>Let(
[
// query load
r1 = MBS( "SystemInfo.CPULoad" );

// separate values
system1 = JSONGetElement ( r1; "system" );
idle1 = JSONGetElement ( r1; "idle" );
user1 = JSONGetElement ( r1; "user" );
total1 = user1+idle1+user1;

// make a 0.5 second pause
t = MBS("Time.Sleep"; 500);

// now query again
r2 = MBS( "SystemInfo.CPULoad" );

// separate values
system2 = JSONGetElement ( r2; "system" );
idle2 = JSONGetElement ( r2; "idle" );
user2 = JSONGetElement ( r2; "user" );
total2 = user2+idle2+user2;

// calculate deltas
deltaTotal = total2 - total1;
deltaSystem = system2 - system1;
deltaIdle = idle2 - idle1;
deltaUser = user2 - user1;

// and calculate the percentage used
load = (deltaSystem+deltaUser) / deltaTotal
]; load)</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
</fmxmlsnippet>

functions.description: Returns a number containing any additional information about the system. e.g. 1 on Windows XP. This member can be one of the following values:

parameters.name: VER_NT_SERVER
parameters.example: The operating system is Windows Server 2008, Windows Server 2003, or Windows 2000 Server. Note that a server that is also a domain controller is reported as VER_NT_DOMAIN_CONTROLLER, not VER_NT_SERVER.

parameters.name: VER_NT_WORKSTATION
parameters.example: The operating system is Windows Vista, Windows XP Professional, Windows XP Home Edition, or Windows 2000 Professional.

functions.name: SystemInfo.WinServicePackMajor
functions.description: Returns the major version number of the latest Service Pack installed on the system. For example, for Service Pack 3, the major version number is 3. If no Service Pack has been installed, the value is zero.

functions.name: SystemInfo.WinServicePackMinor
functions.description: Returns the minor version number of the latest Service Pack installed on the system. For example, for Service Pack 3, the minor version number is 0.

functions.name: SystemInfo.WinSuiteMask
functions.description: Returns a bit mask that identifies the product suites available on the system. for example 256 on Windows XP. This member can be a combination of the following values.

parameters.name: VER_SUITE_BLADE
parameters.example: Windows Server 2003, Web Edition is installed.

parameters.name: VER_SUITE_COMPUTE_SERVER
parameters.example: Windows Server 2003, Compute Cluster Edition is installed.

parameters.name: VER_SUITE_DATACENTER
parameters.example: Windows Server 2008 Datacenter, Windows Server 2003, Datacenter Edition, or Windows 2000 Datacenter Server is installed.

parameters.name: VER_SUITE_ENTERPRISE
parameters.example: Windows Server 2008 Enterprise, Windows Server 2003, Enterprise Edition, or Windows 2000 Advanced Server is installed. Refer to the Remarks section for more information about this bit flag.

parameters.name: VER_SUITE_PERSONAL
parameters.example: Windows Vista Home Premium, Windows Vista Home Basic, or Windows XP Home Edition is installed.

parameters.name: VER_SUITE_SINGLEUSERTS
parameters.example: Remote Desktop is supported, but only one interactive session is supported. This value is set unless the system is running in application server mode.

parameters.name: VER_SUITE_SMALLBUSINESS
parameters.example: Microsoft Small Business Server was once installed on the system, but may have been upgraded to another version of Windows. Refer to the Remarks section for more information about this bit flag.

parameters.name: VER_SUITE_SMALLBUSINESS_RESTRICTED
parameters.example: Microsoft Small Business Server is installed with the restrictive client license in force. Refer to the Remarks section for more information about this bit flag.

parameters.name: VER_SUITE_STORAGE_SERVER
parameters.example: Windows Storage Server 2003 R2 or Windows Storage Server 2003is installed.

parameters.name: VER_SUITE_TERMINAL
parameters.example: Terminal Services is installed. This value is always set. If VER_SUITE_TERMINAL is set but VER_SUITE_SINGLEUSERTS is not set, the system is running in application server mode.

functions.name: WMFP.Create
functions.description: Creates a new player. The player can be audio only without showing in the layout or reference a layout object to play with video. The file is loaded asynchronously, so please wait a few milliseconds or check state later. Use WMFP.Release later to destroy the video player. Pass no window reference and no control name to create an audio player for background playback. See also AVPlayer.OpenContainer and AVPlayer.OpenFile for macOS and iOS.

parameters.name: URL
parameters.description: The URL for the video. See Path.FilePathToFileURL function to convert file path.

parameters.name: WindowRef
parameters.description: Window Reference is the unique OS level window ID. You can obtain this by using the Window.FindByTitle or Window.FindByIndex functions. Pass zero to access the frontmost window.

parameters.name: ControlName
parameters.description: The name of the control on your FileMaker form. e.g. you can place a rectangle there to define the position.

examples.label: Load video into new player:
examples.text_code:
# Create new player and load video
Set Variable [
$URL
; Value:
MBS
( "
Path.FilePathToFileURL
";
Windows Player::Path
) ]
# Player is a rectangle on the layout
Set Variable [
$$player
; Value:
MBS
("WMFP.Create";
$URL
; 0; "Player") ]
If [
MBS
("IsError") ]
Show Custom Dialog [ "Failed to load video" ;
$$player
]
Set Variable [
$$player
; Value: "" ]
Else
# Little pause to let loading happen in background
Pause/Resume Script [ Duration (seconds): ,1 ]
Set Variable [
$r
; Value:
MBS
("
WMFP.SetPlaybackEndedScriptTrigger
";
$$player
; Get(FileName); "Playback Done") ]
Set Variable [
$r
; Value:
MBS
("
WMFP.Play
";
$$player
) ]
End If
Load video into new player:
examples.xml_code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text> Create new player and load video</Text>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS( "Path.FilePathToFileURL"; Windows Player::Path) </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$URL</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text> Player is a rectangle on the layout</Text>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS("WMFP.Create"; $URL; 0; "Player") </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$$player</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="68" name="If">
    <Restore state="False"/>
    <Calculation> MBS("IsError") </Calculation>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="87" name="Show Custom Dialog">
    <Title>
      <Calculation> "Failed to load video" </Calculation>
    </Title>
    <Message>
      <Calculation>$$player </Calculation>
    </Message>
    <Buttons>
      <Button CommitState="True">
        <Calculation>"OK"</Calculation>
      </Button>
      <Button CommitState="False">
        <Calculation>"Cancel"</Calculation>
      </Button>
      <Button CommitState="False"/>
    </Buttons>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>"" </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$$player</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="69" name="Else">
    <Restore state="False"/>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="89" name="# (comment)">
    <Text> Little pause to let loading happen in background</Text>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="62" name="Pause/Resume Script">
    <PauseTime value="ForDuration"/>
    <Calculation>,1 </Calculation>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS("WMFP.SetPlaybackEndedScriptTrigger"; $$player; Get(FileName); "Playback Done") </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS("WMFP.Play"; $$player) </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="70" name="End If"/>
</fmxmlsnippet>

functions.name: WMFP.GetVideoFrameRate
functions.description: Frame rate of a video media type, in frames per second. Requires a media item being loaded into the player. The frame rate is expressed as a ratio. The upper 32 bits of the attribute value contain the numerator and the lower 32 bits contain the denominator. For example, if the frame rate is 30 frames per second (fps), the ratio is 30/1. If the frame rate is 29.97 fps, the ratio is 30,000/1001.

parameters.name: Player
parameters.description: The reference number for the Windows Media Foundation Player object.

examples.label: Query it:
examples.text_code:
Set Variable [
$num
; Value:
MBS
("WMFP.GetVideoFrameRate";
$$player
) ]
Set Variable [
$t
; Value:
MBS
( "
Math.BitwiseShiftRight
";
$num
; 32) ]
Set Variable [
$b
; Value:
MBS
( "
Math.BitwiseAND
";
$num
; 4294967295)]
Set Variable [
$value
; Value:
$t
/
$b
]
Query it:
Example result:
29.97
examples.xml_code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS("WMFP.GetVideoFrameRate"; $$player) </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$num</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS( "Math.BitwiseShiftRight"; $num; 32) </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$t</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS( "Math.BitwiseAnd"; $num; 4294967295)</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$b</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>$t / $b </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$value</Name>
  </Step>
</fmxmlsnippet>

functions.name: X509.Write
functions.description: Writes certificate. Provides either PEM file as text or DER file base64 encoded.

parameters.name: X509Ref
parameters.description: The reference to the X509 certificate.

parameters.name: Binary
parameters.description: Whether to return binary representation (DER format) instead of text (PEM format). Default is PEM.

examples.label: Calculate x5t for a certificate file:
examples.xml_code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>Let ( [
// read PEM file
cert = MBS( "X509.ReadFromFile"; "/Users/cs/Downloads/Cert.pem" );
// write DER file
data = MBS( "X509.Write"; cert; 1 );
// and free memory
r = MBS( "X509.Release"; cert );
// hash it to get x5t
hash = MBS( "Hash.Digest"; "SHA1"; "Base64"; data; ""; "base64url")
]; hash )</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
</fmxmlsnippet>
